Macrons

Consonantal i

Construction, trades & building materials

scaffold platform noun

also platform, deck, working deck, walk-boards

classical

Vitruvius 10.13.4: a siege tower tabulātōrum decem

tabulātum, tabulātī n.

noun, second declension

planked flooring, floor or platform

Applied here to the scaffold’s working deck. A metal deck is a modern application of the platform vocabulary, not evidence that ancient platforms used the same fittings. This is vocabulary for describing the scene, not an assembly specification.

Examples

  • Operārius super tabulātum ambulat.

    The worker is walking on the platform.composed

Other words

  • pontēs — high gangways

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical · Vergil, A. 9.530: turris erat vastō suspectū et pontibus altīs

    A poetic model for walk-boards.

See also storey, board, guardrail, scaffold, ladder.

SourcesLewis & Short: tabulatus · Lewis & Short: pons

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
